concepts.name: Flaked stone tools
concepts.summary: Striking sharp flakes from a stone core to make cutting edges.

concepts.name: Ground-edge stone axe
concepts.summary: Shaping and sharpening a stone axe head by grinding it against abrasive rock, usually for hafting.

concepts.name: Woodworking
concepts.summary: Cutting, shaping and fitting timber into tools and structures.

concepts.name: Cordage
concepts.summary: Twisting or plying plant or animal fibres into string and rope.

concepts.name: Basketry and twined fibre work
concepts.summary: Interlacing, twining or coiling plant fibres into containers, mats and flexible fabrics without a loom.

concepts.name: Mineral pigment paint-making
concepts.summary: Grinding mineral pigments such as ochre and mixing them with binders to make a paint that can be stored and applied.

concepts.name: Lacquer
concepts.summary: Coating wood, fibre or other bodies with refined tree sap that cures to a hard, waterproof film.

concepts.name: Indigo dyeing
concepts.summary: Dyeing fibre blue by fermenting indigo-bearing plants into a soluble vat that oxidises on the cloth.

concepts.name: Mordant dyeing
concepts.summary: Fixing plant dyes fast to fibre, especially cotton, with metal salts such as alum.

concepts.name: Synthetic dyes
concepts.summary: Making dyes by chemical synthesis from coal-tar or petroleum compounds instead of extracting them from plants and animals.

concepts.name: Pottery
concepts.summary: Shaping clay into vessels and firing them so they hold liquids and withstand heat.

concepts.name: Potter's wheel
concepts.summary: Forming clay vessels on a rotating platform, using its momentum to shape them quickly and evenly.

concepts.name: Faience and early glazes
concepts.summary: Giving a quartz or stone body a fused glassy coating, the first deliberately made vitreous material.

concepts.name: High-fired glazed stoneware and porcelain
concepts.summary: Firing selected clays above about 1200 degrees Celsius so the body vitrifies and bonds with a glaze.

concepts.name: Fired brick
concepts.summary: Kiln-firing moulded clay blocks into durable, water-resistant building units.

concepts.name: Glassmaking
concepts.summary: Melting silica with a flux into glass that can be worked into beads, vessels and sheets.

concepts.name: Glassblowing
concepts.summary: Inflating molten glass on the end of a hollow tube to form thin-walled vessels quickly.

concepts.name: Lost-wax casting
concepts.summary: Casting metal in a mould formed around a wax model that is melted out before pouring.

concepts.name: Tin bronze
concepts.summary: Deliberately alloying copper with tin to make a harder, more castable metal.

concepts.name: Iron smelting
concepts.summary: Reducing iron ore with charcoal in a furnace to produce workable iron.

concepts.name: Blast-furnace cast iron
concepts.summary: Smelting iron ore in a tall, strongly blown furnace hot enough to yield liquid iron that can be cast.

concepts.name: Crucible steel
concepts.summary: Making homogeneous high-carbon steel by melting iron with carbon in sealed crucibles.

concepts.name: Coke iron smelting
concepts.summary: Smelting iron with coke made from mineral coal in place of charcoal.

concepts.name: Stainless steel
concepts.summary: Alloying steel with enough chromium that a self-healing surface film stops it rusting.

concepts.name: Salt production
concepts.summary: Obtaining salt in quantity by boiling or evaporating brine or by mining rock salt.

concepts.name: Deep borehole drilling
concepts.summary: Sinking narrow lined boreholes hundreds of metres deep with a percussion bit to reach brine, gas or oil.

concepts.name: Petroleum well drilling
concepts.summary: Drilling wells specifically to produce crude oil in commercial quantity.

concepts.name: Silver amalgamation
concepts.summary: Extracting silver from crushed low-grade ore at scale by reacting it with mercury and salts.

concepts.name: Loom weaving
concepts.summary: Interlacing spun warp and weft threads under tension on a frame to make cloth.

concepts.name: Cotton textiles
concepts.summary: Ginning, spinning and weaving the short seed fibres of cotton into cloth.

concepts.name: Sericulture and silk
concepts.summary: Rearing silkworms and reeling the continuous filament of their cocoons into thread for weaving.

concepts.name: Barkcloth
concepts.summary: Making cloth without weaving by soaking and beating the inner bark of trees into wide felted sheets.

concepts.name: Spinning wheel
concepts.summary: Spinning thread on a spindle turned by a hand- or foot-driven wheel instead of a dropped spindle.

concepts.name: Power loom
concepts.summary: Weaving cloth on a loom whose shedding, picking and beating are driven by water or steam power.

concepts.name: Papyrus sheet
concepts.summary: Making a smooth writing sheet by laying and pressing strips of papyrus pith in crossed layers.

concepts.name: Beaten bark paper
concepts.summary: Making a writing and ritual sheet by boiling and beating inner tree bark flat, then coating it.

concepts.name: Wood-pulp paper
concepts.summary: Making paper from wood reduced to fibre by grinding or chemical cooking, in place of rags.

concepts.name: Lime burning
concepts.summary: Heating limestone to quicklime and slaking it to make plaster, mortar and a strong alkali.

concepts.name: Distillation
concepts.summary: Separating and concentrating liquids by boiling them and condensing the vapour in a purpose-built still.

concepts.name: Mineral acids
concepts.summary: Preparing strong acids such as nitric and sulfuric acid by distilling mineral salts.

concepts.name: Industrial sulfuric acid
concepts.summary: Making sulfuric acid cheaply and in bulk as a feedstock for other chemical industries.

concepts.name: Superphosphate fertiliser
concepts.summary: Treating bones or phosphate rock with sulfuric acid to make a soluble manufactured fertiliser.

concepts.name: Phenol-formaldehyde resin
concepts.summary: A fully synthetic plastic made by condensing phenol with formaldehyde and setting it hard under heat and pressure.

concepts.name: Polyethylene
concepts.summary: Polymerising ethylene gas into a tough, flexible, insulating thermoplastic.

concepts.name: Polyester fibre
concepts.summary: Spinning polyethylene terephthalate into a strong synthetic textile fibre.

concepts.name: Semiconductor single crystals
concepts.summary: Growing large, ultra-pure single crystals of germanium or silicon with controlled doping.

concepts.name: Neodymium-iron-boron magnet
concepts.summary: A permanent magnet of neodymium, iron and boron with far higher energy density than earlier magnets.

origins.title: Flaked stone tools in East Africa
origins.where: Rift Valley of Kenya and Ethiopia (West Turkana, Gona, Ledi-Geraru, Nyayanga)
origins.why: Every later hominin toolkit, and with it butchery, woodworking and the whole stone age, descends from deliberately struck sharp flakes.
origins.verify: Pin down the earliest secure dated assemblage: whether the 3.3 million-year-old Lomekwi 3 pieces are accepted as deliberate knapping, and the dates and sites of the earliest Oldowan (Gona, Ledi-Geraru, Nyayanga). Say which hominins are associated and how firm that is.

origins.title: Ground-edge stone axes in northern Australia
origins.where: Kimberley and Arnhem Land, northern Australia
origins.why: Hafted axes with ground edges gave the first Australians a durable woodworking tool tens of thousands of years before ground stone appeared in the Neolithic elsewhere.
origins.verify: Confirm the earliest secure ground-edge axe evidence (Carpenter's Gap 1, Nawarla Gabarnmang, the contested Madjedbebe dates) and how long the tradition stayed confined to the tropical north. Note the separate Japanese Palaeolithic edge-ground axes of c. 38,000 years ago, which may deserve their own record as an independent origin.

origins.title: Woodworking in Middle Pleistocene south-central Africa
origins.where: Kalambo Falls, Zambia
origins.why: Shaped and notched logs show hominins building with timber long before Homo sapiens, the root of digging sticks, spears, shelters and every later wooden technology.
origins.verify: Check the luminescence dating and interpretation of the interlocking logs and wooden tools at Kalambo Falls, and place them against other early worked wood (Clacton, Schoningen, Gesher Benot Ya'aqov). Wood almost never survives, so state how far the date is a minimum.

origins.title: Twisted fibre cordage in Middle Palaeolithic France

origins.verify: Confirm the dating and the identification of the three-ply bast cord fragment at Abri du Maras and its attribution to Neanderthals. List the next oldest direct finds (Ohalo II, Lascaux) and the indirect evidence (perforated beads, use-wear) that points much earlier in Africa, so the record can say how far cordage among Homo sapiens was a separate development.
